Hi Samira — thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion, wanted to send a short recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. I’ve also attached a quick SLO worksheet that maps the targets you mentioned to potential Redwood deployment options.

Recap of pain points / goals (as we heard them):
- Production doc summarization workload with interactive editor UX (users expect near-instant feedback).
- p95 latency target: <=120ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens); p99 target: <=250ms.
- Peak throughput: 60 concurrent active users generating ~12 qps sustained, occasional bursts up to ~80 qps.
- Model requirements: fine-tuned Llama-2-70B instruction variant for in-house docs, 8k token context, ability to preserve chains-of-thought for multi-step edits.
- Privacy/regulatory: must run in a VPC with customer-managed keys; audit logs required for compliance.

What we recommend (high level):
1) Deployment topology: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) inside your VPC with a 3-node GPU pool (A100/80GB or equivalent) fronted by a lightweight router. Each node runs two model replicas with dynamic KV cache sharing. This gives headroom for 60-80 qps with low tail latencies.
2) Serving config: mixed-precision quantized model (4-bit PTQ) + kernel selection tuned for 8k context; continuous batching with a short 5-10ms scheduling window for throughput efficiency while protecting p99.
3) Caching/batching: prefix KV cache for common prompts and session affinity to reduce repeated context decoding.
4) Fallbacks: can route burst traffic to a lower-cost Llama-2-13B variant for non-critical completions to maintain SLOs during overload.
5) Security/compliance: Private deployment with KMS integration, per-request audit logs, and SOC2 artifacts — we’ll loop security as needed.

Open questions (from our side):
- Can you confirm the 8k context requirement is a hard constraint for all flows, or only for long-document batches?
- Expected average tokens per request and per response (estimates will help sizing).
- Any additional network constraints (e.g., egress restrictions, static IP requirements)?

Next steps:
- Dev and Mateo will validate sizing and put together a short reference topology (+ cost estimate) by EOD Thursday.
- We’ll schedule a 45-min follow-up to walk the topology and failover strategy — how does Friday 10am PT look for your team?

Attachments: SLO_worksheet_FINEX.xlsx, redwood-architecture-diagram.png

Thanks — appreciate the time today.

Quick notes from my side after a fast sizing pass:

- The 3-node A100 pool is a reasonable starting point but borderline on p99 for 8k context at peak burst if all requests hit full context. With quantized 4-bit and optimized kernels we estimate:
  - p95: ~90-110ms for 512-token short prompts
  - p99: ~200-260ms for 8k flows depending on batching window (5-10ms) and session affinity.
- Recommendations:
  1) Start with 4 x A100 instances (gives more headroom and smoother p99) and expose an autoscale policy for scheduled off-peak downscale.
  2) Use shared KV cache across replicas with session affinity to keep tail latencies down for interactive sessions.
  3) Offer model variant routing: Llama-2-70B quantized for critical paths, fallback to 13B for background/bulk jobs.
  4) Provide static egress IPs via NAT gateway in the VPC and ensure KMS integration for keys.

I’ll run a short perf sim and share numbers + diagram (will push redwood-architecture-diagram.png to the Drive link). If this looks good I can join Friday’s call to walk the topology.
